title: Three Innovations We Need Right Now
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant discuss three "innovations we need right now": teleportation, a universal language, and whole-brain innovators/renaissance scientists. The teleportation segment covers the term's origin (Charles Fort), quantum teleportation of atoms and photons, quantum entanglement, Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, Charles Bennett's view, and benefits such as commuting and shipping goods. The universal language segment covers L. L. Zamenhof and Esperanto (structural vs. symbolic approaches, Shatner film Incubus, claimed two million speakers) and the benefits for trade and science. The innovator segment covers renaissance scientists, the narrowing of graduate education, and figures such as Edward Witten, Murray Gell-Mann, Stephen Hawking, and Bill Gates. The episode closes with a listener mail segment from Australia, Serbia, and China (including the Great Firewall blocking of the show and blog) and the sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and setup
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode, joke about Chuck's stopwatch to keep the talk short, and frame the topic as three innovations the world needs, inviting blog feedback.

segments.title: Teleportation
segments.summary: The hosts discuss teleportation, its origin in Charles Fort's writing, and how it would work by scanning and recreating a person rather than moving atoms. They cover the destruction of the original, the soul question, quantum entanglement, Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, Charles Bennett's view, and benefits such as shorter commutes and cheaper shipping of goods.

segments.title: Universal language and Esperanto
segments.summary: The hosts argue that language barriers fuel conflict and misunderstanding. They discuss L. L. Zamenhof's creation of Esperanto, its structural and symbolic design challenges, its roughly two million speakers, and the film Incubus shot in Esperanto with William Shatner. They also cover the economic and scientific benefits of a shared language.

segments.title: Renaissance scientists and whole-brain innovators
segments.summary: The hosts argue the world needs whole-brain thinkers and renaissance scientists, and that graduate education narrows students toward specific funded research. They name candidates including Edward Witten, Murray Gell-Mann, Stephen Hawking, and Bill Gates.

segments.title: Listener mail from Australia, Serbia, and China
segments.summary: The hosts read emails from Nicola in Australia, Luca in Serbia (correcting the claim that Nicola Tesla was Austrian; he was an ethnic Serb), and Yao Jian in China, who reports that the show and blog are blocked by the Great Firewall.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck invite listeners to send feedback and corrections by email and point to the HowStuffWorks website.
